## Overview

`generate_report()` bundles everything into one HTML file, but every plot and
table in NanoQuRe is also available as a standalone function. This is useful
for embedding a specific plot in an R Markdown document, adjusting its
parameters, or inspecting a single metric interactively.

Each function takes a data frame with the reads of one sample and stops with
a message naming the missing columns when the input is incomplete. The
`passes_filtering` column has to be logical here; only `generate_report()`
converts text or 1/0 flags.

```{r load-data}
library(NanoQuRe)

data(sample_data)
```

---

## Summary tables

### `sequencing_stats()`

Returns a one-row summary of the run: duration, number of reads, total bases
sequenced, percentage of passed reads, and average translocation speed
[nt/s]. The speed is the total read length divided by the summed read
duration.

```{r sequencing-stats}
sequencing_stats(sample_data)
```

### `quality_stats()`

Returns the main quality metrics: total and passed read counts, N50, mean
Q-score, longest read, and mean length of passed reads. Missing values are
ignored in both tables.

```{r quality-stats}
quality_stats(sample_data)
```

### `calculate_n50()`

Returns the N50 value alone, without a table or a plot:

```{r n50}
calculate_n50(sample_data)
```

---

## Yield and throughput

### `plot_cumulative_yield()`

Shows how the sequenced bases accumulate over the run, separately for pass and
fail reads. A flattening curve suggests that output is declining.

```{r cumulative-yield}
plot_cumulative_yield(sample_data)
```

### `plot_seq_throughput()`

Shows the yield per hour instead of the cumulative yield. Each read is
assigned to the hour in which it started, and hours without reads are shown
as zero yield. The plot may help to spot periods of low output during the
run.

```{r seq-throughput}
plot_seq_throughput(sample_data)
```

### `plot_average_speed()`

Shows the translocation speed per hour in nt/s (summed read length divided by
summed read duration), separately for pass and fail reads. Hours without
reads appear as gaps in the line. A drop in speed can indicate pore ageing or
buffer depletion, although the summary alone does not identify the cause.

```{r average-speed}
plot_average_speed(sample_data)
```

---

## Read length and quality

### `plot_read_lengths()`

Plots a histogram of read lengths on a log10 axis, with vertical lines for
the mean read length and the N50 value. By default each bar is the number of
reads in a length bin; `weight = "bases"` shows the number of bases instead,
i.e. where the sequenced bases are. `upper_limit` sets the x-axis maximum;
reads beyond it are counted in a note on the plot. `log_x = FALSE` switches
to a linear axis, on which the bins are sized to the visible range.

```{r read-lengths}
plot_read_lengths(sample_data)
```

```{r read-lengths-custom, eval = FALSE}
# bases per length bin, on a linear axis up to 20 kb
plot_read_lengths(sample_data, weight = "bases", log_x = FALSE, upper_limit = 20000)
```

### `plot_quality_distribution()`

Plots the Q-score distribution of pass and fail reads over the full range of
scores. Up to two vertical lines are shown: a user-defined cut-off for
downstream analysis (`qscore_cutoff`, Q7 by default) and, only when both pass
and fail reads exist, the pass/fail threshold of the basecaller as derived
from the data.

```{r quality-distribution}
plot_quality_distribution(sample_data, qscore_cutoff = 7)
```

### `plot_double()`

Returns a named list of two plots, `length_plot` and `qscore_plot`, with the
minimum, mean, and maximum read length and Q-score per hour of the run.

```{r double}
double_plots <- plot_double(sample_data)
double_plots$length_plot
double_plots$qscore_plot
```

---

## Channel activity

### `plot_active_channels()`

Shows how many channels produced at least one read in each time window
(10 minutes by default, set with `bin_width` in hours). Dashed lines mark
the first window in which this number falls to 50% and 25% of the highest
count in the first hour (`thresholds`); the final, usually partial, window is
not considered. Pore scans and pauses are not recorded in the sequencing
summary, so short dips or gaps can reflect run control and not pore loss.

```{r active-channels}
plot_active_channels(sample_data)
```

### `pore_activity_heatmap()`

Shows two complementary views of channel yield: a heatmap of channels over
time (`bin_width` in hours, 1 by default) and a heatmap on the flow cell
layout. A darker colour means more bases sequenced through that channel.
`platform` selects the layout: `"minion"` (512 channels, default) or
`"promethion"` (3000 channels). The input has to contain a single `run_id`,
channel numbers outside the selected layout stop the function, and Flongle
flow cells are not supported.

```{r pore-heatmap}
pore_activity_heatmap(sample_data, platform = "minion")
```
